name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with

157-
158-Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
159-exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from Figma and from

161-only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

163-1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
164-   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
165-   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
166-   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
167-   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
168-   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
169-   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
170-   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
171-   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.

173-   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a

175-   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

content.text:
My review of the code is done, and the Mac build is still compiling at step 218 of 866. Here is what reading the change shows. The Mac run results will follow when the build finishes.

## Verdict so far

The branch does what was decided. The saved-spool code is gone, and the chip and menu read only what OrcaSlicer stores. Four things the coding agent did not highlight need your attention. One is a possible crash on the Mac that I have not reproduced yet.

## Not highlighted by the coding agent

| Finding | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| "Other filament…" opens OrcaSlicer's setup wizard page of checkboxes | Frame 23c drew a search inside the menu. The wizard installs a filament but does not select it, so the person must pick it again afterwards |
| The menu rebuilds all its rows on every click | A Mac-only crash was seen on 2026-09-09 when menu rows were rebuilt under the pointer. I found no fix for it on this branch |
| Dot sizes, gaps and fade strength are typed as numbers in the code | The project rule is to add a design token first, never a typed number |
| Opening the colour picker ends the menu visit | One visit can produce two chat lines instead of one |
| Verified on Windows only | No Mac or Linux run is recorded |

The commit message also carries a co-author line.

## The coding agent's own points

| Point | My view |
|---|---|
| Hover shows text only | Acceptable. A system tooltip cannot draw swatches |
| Empty plate shows every slot as in use | I agree with it. The brief had no rule for an empty plate, and a lone faded dot would look disabled |
| Colour cells work with the mouse only | Should be fixed. The design system requires keyboard access |
| Dot drawn before the slot number | Cosmetic. The design puts the number first |
| Frame 23b-2's caption is wrong | Correct. OrcaSlicer applies a preset's default colour when it has one. 582 of 7,053 shipped presets do |

## Gaps from earlier that are now closed

- A nozzle change now re-picks a filament that no longer fits.
- The printer setup chat no longer stores spools.
- Home shows loaded filament only for a connected printer.
- The sync dialog opened with the sidebar hidden, per the Windows test run.

## Still running

I created my own copy of the branch and started a Mac build. When it finishes I will run the unit tests and the test harness, then click through the menu to see whether the crash happens.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_ax_find
entries.description:
Search the accessibility elements captured by the last app_screenshot of one window. Filter by role (e.g. "AXTextArea", "AXButton") and/or title substring. Returns matching elements with their [N] index — pass that as element_index to app_click/app_type. Use this when the inline summary in app_screenshot doesn't show the element you need (it only lists the first few actionable ones).

This tool acts on one application in the BACKGROUND while the user keeps working in other apps. The target window does not come to the front. For the menu bar use app_menu; hover states and context menus still need the display-scope screenshot/left_click tools (which do take over the screen).

app.description: Bundle identifier of the target application (e.g. "com.apple.TextEdit"). Must be in the granted-applications list — call request_access first if it isn't.

window_id.description: CGWindowID from app_list_windows or from a previous app_screenshot result. If omitted, defaults to the window you most recently app_screenshot-ed for this app (or the app's main window if you haven't screenshotted yet). Pass a different id to switch windows — there is no separate switch-window tool; targeting is per-call via this parameter.

role.description: Exact AX role to match (e.g. "AXButton", "AXTextArea", "AXLink", "AXComboBox"). Omit to match any role.

title_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring to match against the element's title. Omit to match any title.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_batch
entries.description:
Execute a sequence of app_* actions against ONE window in a single tool call. Each individual app_* call is a model→API round trip; batching a predictable sequence (e.g. click a field, type into it, press return) eliminates all but one. Actions execute sequentially and stop on the first error or 'unsupported' result. An 'ineffective' result (write accepted, app didn't visibly respond yet) does NOT stop the batch — include a screenshot action after to verify. Include {"action":"screenshot"} anywhere in the list to capture the window at that point — coordinates and element_index in actions AFTER a screenshot refer to that screenshot. Put one last to see the post-batch state in the same call.

coordinate.description: (x, y) in pixels of the most recent app_screenshot's full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled app_screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones — the AX summary lines use the same space). (0, 0) is the frame's top-left corner; an app_screenshot of the window is required first. Mutually exclusive with element_index and target.

element_index.description: Index into the AX summary returned by the last app_screenshot (the [N] prefix on each line). Targets that element's center directly instead of by coordinate. Use when coordinate-based clicking returns unsupported(canvas). Mutually exclusive with coordinate and target.

scale.description: For screenshot and zoom only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

region.description: For zoom only. [x0, y0, x1, y1]: left, top, right, bottom edges of the region, in pixels of the most recent app_screenshot's full-resolution coordinate frame (same space as `coordinate`).

target.description:
Dispatch against the application's currently-focused UI element (AXFocusedUIElement) instead of hit-testing at a coordinate. Use for canvas-heavy apps (Pages, Keynote) where the document body has no positional accessibility elements but the app's own text cursor is somewhere editable. Mutually exclusive with coordinate and element_index.

If you omit ALL of coordinate, element_index, and target, the action defaults to the same point as your most recent app_* action on this window — so [click coord, type text, key combo] chains naturally without repeating the coordinate.

to_coordinate.description: Drag endpoint (window-local coord). A 'drag' needs this or `path`.

path.description: For drag only: [[x, y], ...] points to drag through, first = press, last = release; replaces coordinate + to_coordinate.

actions.description: e.g. [{"action":"click","coordinate":[100,200]},{"action":"type","text":"hello"},{"action":"key","combo":"return"},{"action":"screenshot"}] — type/key default to the point the previous action used.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_bring_to_current_space
entries.description: Bring one of this app's windows from another desktop Space onto the CURRENT Space, so you can act on it in the background. Use this when an action told you a window is off-Space and this app can't be controlled there — apps that only accept input when brought to the front (which would flash on-screen). The window appears on the user's desktop (visible to them, but the app does NOT take focus) and becomes actionable — take a fresh app_screenshot next. If the window is already on the current Space this is a no-op. Requires an app grant; refused while the screen is locked.

entries.description:

Target by coordinate, element_index, or target: 'focused' (writes to the app's currently-focused text element — use this for Pages/Keynote-style apps where the document body is a canvas). Replaces the current selection. Only target TEXT fields: typing at a pop-up button, dropdown, or other non-text control is refused (the text would land in whatever field has keyboard focus instead).

target.description:
Dispatch against the application's currently-focused UI element (AXFocusedUIElement) instead of hit-testing at a coordinate. Use for canvas-heavy apps (Pages, Keynote) where the document body has no positional accessibility elements but the app's own text cursor is somewhere editable. Mutually exclusive with coordinate and element_index.

If you omit ALL of coordinate, element_index, and target, the action defaults to the same point as your most recent app_* action on this window — so [click coord, type text, key combo] chains naturally without repeating the coordinate.

overwrite_existing.description: Only relevant when positional insert (set AXSelectedText) doesn't work for this app and the field already has content — in that case the only background fallback is replacing the WHOLE field. By default that is REFUSED (unsupported: would_replace_content) so you don't clobber a draft or document. Set true to proceed; the previous content (≤500 chars) is returned in the result so you can restore it if the replace was wrong.

mode.description: insert (default) writes at the caret/selection. replace selects all then writes, clearing the field in one call — use when you need to overwrite the whole field rather than append.

disable_substitutions.description: Disable the app's Text Replacement / autocorrect around this type (so e.g. "backpropagation" is not mangled), then restore the user's prior setting afterward.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__computer_batch
entries.description: Execute a sequence of actions in ONE tool call. Each individual tool call requires a model→API round trip (seconds); batching a predictable sequence eliminates all but one. Use this whenever you can predict the outcome of several actions ahead — e.g. click a field, type into it, press Return. Actions execute sequentially and stop on the first error. The frontmost application must be in the session allowlist at the time of this call, or this tool returns an error and does nothing. The frontmost check runs before EACH action inside the batch — if an action opens a non-allowed app, the next action's gate fires and the batch stops there. Screenshot and zoom actions are allowed and their images are returned interleaved with the per-action outputs. Coordinates you write in THIS batch — clicks AND zoom regions — always refer to the full-screen screenshot taken BEFORE this call, never to a zoom and never to a mid-batch screenshot. After the batch returns, the most recent full screenshot it produced becomes the new coordinate reference for your next call. IMPORTANT: in this session the individual interaction tools (left_click, type, key, scroll, drag, etc.) are NOT available — this is the ONLY way to click, type, or otherwise interact with the computer. A single action is just a one-item batch.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__teach_batch
entries.description: Queue multiple teach steps in one tool call. Parallels computer_batch: N steps → one model↔API round trip instead of N. The branch is not ready to merge yet. The feature works on the Mac and matches the design in its main path, but I reproduced a crash there, and one design departure needs your decision. I built the branch in my own copy and ran it on this Mac.

## Mac results

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Unit tests | 52 cases pass |
| Test harness, default run | 431 checks pass, 3 fail |
| Menu appearance | Matches frame 23b: title, colour row, installed list, three quiet rows |
| Crash probe | 1 crash in 7 runs |

The three failing checks:

- **Print preflight.** The coding agent says this fails without the change too. I did not verify that on the Mac.
- **Two colour-click checks.** The fault is in the test, which clicks the wrong position on the Mac. A correctly placed click changes the colour.

## The crash

I added a temporary probe to my copy of the test harness. It sends what the Mac sends: the pointer moves over a row, the row is clicked, the pointer moves again. One run in seven ended in a segmentation fault at the second move. I did not capture a stack.

My reading of the cause: the popup keeps a pointer to the row under the pointer, and the new menu destroys and rebuilds every row on each click. Nothing clears that pointer. The same crash was recorded on 2026-09-09.

## Findings, most serious first

| Finding | Kind |
|---|---|
| Intermittent crash on the Mac after a row click | Must fix |
| "Other filament…" opens OrcaSlicer's setup wizard, not the search in frame 23c | Your decision |
| On a new install the colour row holds only the current colour and "+" | Your decision |
| Colour cells cannot be reached by keyboard | Fix |
| Dot sizes, gaps and fade strength are typed numbers, not design tokens | Fix |
| The colour-click test uses the wrong position on the Mac | Fix the test |
| Opening the colour picker can split one visit into two chat lines | Minor |
| Dot drawn before the slot number | Cosmetic |
| Commit message carries a co-author line | Minor |

On the colour row: OrcaSlicer ships no saved colours, so a first colour change always goes through the system picker.

## Not checked

- The filament list on a printer with two nozzle sizes.
- The sync dialog on the Mac. I ran only the default harness mode.
- Real pointer clicks. The screen tools could not drive this popup in the background.

## Where things are

- My copy of the branch: `.claude/worktrees/review-filament-chip`, with a 13 GB build. I restored it to match the branch.
- The probe, as a patch: `pointer-move-probe.patch` in this session's scratchpad folder.

Here are the four problems written for the coding agent, ready to paste. Line numbers refer to commit `a74862697e` on branch `claude/filament-chip`. I found problems 1, 2 and 4 by reading the code and seeing the menu on the Mac. Problem 3 comes from reading the code only, so the agent should reproduce it first.

````markdown
# Four fixes for the filament chip (branch claude/filament-chip)

All paths are under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/` unless stated.
Line numbers are at commit a74862697e.

## 1. Colour cells cannot be reached by keyboard

**What is wrong.** In the filament menu, the colour swatches and the "+" cell
respond to the mouse only. A person using the keyboard can change the filament
but not the colour.

**Where.**
- `FilamentMenu.cpp:64` `ColourCell` binds enter, leave and left-button-up, and
  nothing for keys or focus.
- `HeaderControls.cpp:663` `HeaderMenu::on_key` moves only through `m_items`,
  the row buttons. The colour row is built by `set_header_builder`, so it is
  never in that list.

**Expected.**
- Up from the first filament row moves into the colour row. Down leaves it.
- Left and Right move between cells, including "+".
- Return or Space applies the cell, the same as a click.
- The focused cell shows the 2 DIP focus ring the design system requires.
- After a colour is applied the menu rebuilds. The keyboard position stays on
  the same cell.
- Where a keyboard-opened menu starts does not change.

**How to check.** Add harness checks that send keys through the menu's key
handler: reach a saved colour with arrows, press Return, and confirm the slot's
colour changed and the menu stayed open.

## 2. Sizes typed as numbers instead of design tokens

**What is wrong.** The branch adds sizes as typed numbers. The project rule is
in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`, section "Writing UI code", rules 1
and 2: add the token first, extend the guard, then read it from code.

**Where.** New on this branch:

| Value | Location |
|---|---|
| Slot dot size, 8 and 4 | `HeaderControls.cpp:121-122` |
| Gap between slot dots, 3 and 2 | `HeaderControls.cpp:123-124` |
| Gap from the dots to the label, 8 | `HeaderControls.cpp:263` |
| Fade strength of an unused slot, 90 of 255 | `HeaderControls.cpp:404` |
| Colour cell inset and ring width | `FilamentMenu.cpp:95`, `:102`, `:110` |

Carried over from the old spool menu, still typed: the colour grid gap and
caption gap of 4, at `FilamentMenu.cpp:328` and `:341`.

**Expected.** Each value is a token in
`resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`, read through `ShellTheme::metrics()`,
with a guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp`. Follow the existing
`component.swatch` entry: parsed at `ShellTheme.cpp:267`, held in
`SwatchMetrics` in `ShellTheme.hpp:101`.

**Leave alone.** `kFullSizeDots` and `kColoursPerRow` are counts, not sizes.

**How to check.** The guard test fails when a token is removed or changed. The
chip renders the same as before.

## 3. One menu visit can post two chat lines

**What is wrong.** The design posts one grey chat line per menu visit that
changed a filament. A visit ends whenever the popup is dismissed, including
when the menu closes itself to show a dialog and then reopens.

**Where.**
- `FilamentMenu.cpp:144` every popup gets a dismiss listener that calls
  `end_visit`.
- `FilamentMenu.cpp:372` `pick_colour` closes the popup before the system
  colour picker, then reopens it.
- `FilamentMenu.cpp:290` "Other filament…" closes the popup, opens OrcaSlicer's
  filament page, then reopens it.

**Reproduce first.**
1. Open the filament menu and pick a different filament.
2. Click "+", pick a colour, press OK. The menu comes back.
3. Pick another filament.
4. Click away.

I expect two chat lines. I have not run this by hand.

**Expected.** One line, naming the final filament. A visit ends only when the
person leaves the menu: click-away, Esc, Tab, "Filament settings…", or the
sync row. A close that the menu makes itself, followed by a reopen, is the same
visit. If the menu cannot reopen, end the visit so the line is not lost.

**How to check.** The existing checks `the_visit_leaves_one_line` and
`one_menu_visit_posts_one_note` do not cover a close and reopen in the middle.
Add one that does.

## 4. Dot drawn before the slot number

**What is wrong.** In the slot list, each row reads dot, number, name. The
design, frame 23d, reads number, dot, name.

**Where.** `FilamentMenu.cpp:206-207`. The number is part of the label, and the
colour is the row's leading dot, which is drawn before the label at
`HeaderControls.cpp:393`.

**Expected.** Number first, then the dot, then the filament's short name.

**Keep.** The row's name, used for lookup and accessibility, stays
"1  Bambu PLA Basic". The harness check `the_slot_list_names_each_slot`
depends on it.

**How to check.** Render the slot list to a picture in the harness and confirm
the order. The harness currently photographs only the chip.
````

Two things I left out because you did not ask for them here: the intermittent crash on the Mac, and the "Other filament…" and empty colour row decisions. The crash should be fixed before any of these four, because fix 1 adds more ways to rebuild the menu under the pointer.

Here is the description, ready to paste. It stands alone, so an agent with no knowledge of this session can act on it. I reproduced the failure on this Mac and confirmed the cause with a corrected click.

````markdown
# Fix: the colour-click test clicks the wrong position on macOS

## Summary

Two checks in the shell test harness fail on macOS and pass on Windows. The
app is correct. The test computes the click position wrongly for a control
that sits inside a nested panel. This is a test-only fix.

- Branch: `claude/filament-chip`, commit `a74862697e`
- File: `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`
- Build target: `shell_integration_harness`

## Failing checks

Run the harness with no arguments on macOS. Two checks fail:

| Check | Line |
|---|---|
| `a_colour_click_sets_the_slot_colour` | 3302 |
| `the_line_is_led_by_the_colour` | 3313 |

The second fails only because the first did. The colour never changed, so the
chat line carries the old colour.

A third check, `print_opens_cancellable_native_preflight`, also fails. It is
unrelated. Do not touch it in this fix.

## Background

The filament menu is a popup window. On macOS the popup receives every mouse
event itself and forwards it to the child under the pointer. The code for that
is `PopupWindow::OnMouseEvent2` in `src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/PopupWindow.cpp`.
It finds the child by walking down the window tree and adjusting the position
at each level.

So on macOS the harness posts its click to the popup, at a position measured
from the popup's top-left corner. On Windows it posts to the child directly.

## Cause

`click_row`, at line 2919, computes the macOS position like this:

```cpp
const wxPoint at = row->GetPosition() + wxPoint(row->GetSize().x / 2, row->GetSize().y / 2);
```

`GetPosition()` is measured from the control's own parent. For a menu row the
parent is the popup, so the result is right. A colour cell is different:

- The popup holds a panel, built in `FilamentMenu::build_colour_row`
  (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp:322`).
- The colour cells are children of that panel (`FilamentMenu.cpp:344`).

For a colour cell, `GetPosition()` is measured from the panel, not the popup.
The click lands near the popup's top-left corner and misses the cell.

The call that goes wrong is at line 3298: `click_row(menu, cell);`

## Evidence

I added a temporary probe that computed the position from screen coordinates:

```cpp
child->GetScreenPosition() - popup->GetScreenPosition()
    + wxPoint(child->GetSize().x / 2, child->GetSize().y / 2)
```

With that position, posted to the popup the same way, the slot's colour
changed and the menu stayed open. Two macOS runs, both passed.

## Expected fix

Make `click_row` compute the macOS position relative to the popup for any
````
